card: Excludes private broadcast connections from normal P2P address discouragement on the 31.x release branch while preserving disconnection on misbehavior. The change prevents observable IP discouragement state from deanonymizing private broadcast peers. This is a backport rebase of PR #36312 onto the 31.x maintenance branch.
changed_since_previous: None in the commit itself; a diff is now available, showing base divergence.
evidence: Author states: "Discouraging a private broadcast connection may be observable. Prevent this by keeping private broadcast connections outside normal discouragement handling."
problem: Discouraging an IP address upon misbehavior is observable across network connections and external monitors, which can leak or deanonymize private broadcast connections.

risk.why: Altering peer discouragement behavior in P2P logic could fail to penalize abusive peers or affect node connectivity on private broadcast connections.

scope_notes: The PR contains a single backport commit (+44/-5 in 4 files), but the diff relative to the merge base includes hundreds of unrelated changes due to target branch divergence.
summary: Excludes private broadcast connections from standard peer discouragement handling on the 31.x release branch. Misbehaving private broadcast peers are disconnected immediately without recording their addresses in the discouragement filter.
